en: I bow to the auspicious Śivā, the primordial and venerable Mother of the Vedas, whose speech is most excellent and whose feet are worshipped by the foremost gods and sages; she who is composed of the three worlds,
the supreme power (Parā Śakti), who assumes manifold forms and consists of the qualities (guṇas) in order to create.
I worship Mother Gāyatrī, the supremely fortunate one, the mother who gives birth to bliss.
Pure, established in the strength of all beings, the remover of all miserable and difficult conditions;
formless yet essential, the embodiment of stainless austerity, incomparable;
the eldest in the world, most excellent, worshipped by gods and demons, and praised by the Vedas.
I worship the Mother Gāyatrī, the supremely fortunate one, the progenitor of bliss;
she who is established in austerity, the most desired, the quencher of the mental anguish of her own people,
the embodiment of compassion, the manifestation of splendor, and who is easily attained solely through the grace of constant effort.
I worship that most auspicious Mother Gāyatrī— the most excellent and holy one who removes all the bonds of worldly existence, the supremely fortunate mother of bliss,
who is ever to be propitiated and attained, and who expands the intellect of those possessed of good understanding.

I worship Mother Gāyatrī— the sorrowless, luminous, supreme, divine, and auspicious one who removes the blindness of delusion residing in the heart, the sole boat for crossing the ocean of worldly existence, the most fortunate mother who brings forth bliss.
The unborn, non-dual, triadic, possessing various forms of qualities, perfectly pure,
the destroyer of darkness, the lute with strings whose sound is as sweet as the Vedas, consisting of aesthetic essence,
highly honored, blessed, and eternally endowed with the power of a compassionate nature.
I worship Mother Gāyatrī, the supremely fortunate one, the mother of Nanda,
the sustainer of the universe, the vessel for the destruction of all worldly existence,
the heroic and steadfast one, that path leading to a mass of perfectly pure austerity.
I worship the Mother Gāyatrī— the singular one among the many, the foundation for the three worlds, the most auspicious, the mother of bliss,
the awakened and the awakener— who gives birth to herself and removes the dullness of ignorance.
I worship the blessed Mother Gāyatrī, who is golden-hued, virtuous, praised by excellent poets, most skillful, possessed of true knowledge, irreproachable, whose hymn of pure qualities is stainless,
supremely auspicious, and the mother of bliss.

The multitude of wise ones worship her who is infinite and peaceful, who consists of the Vedas, and who is easy to sing of; the Lord of the Gods constantly remembers her in his heart with devotion and power— she who is ever under the sway of the love of those whose minds are bowed in surrender.
I worship Mother Gāyatrī, the most auspicious, the mother of Nanda;
he who, with a pure mind, recites this auspicious *Gāyatrī-aṣṭaka*,
shall become fortunate in this world, and his mother will be pleased with him.
